newsitem.title: DENMARK: Carlsberg says still in Coke talks.
newsitem.headline: Carlsberg says still in Coke talks.

text.p: Danish brewer Carlsberg said on Thursday it was still negotiating with Coca Cola Company on possible future co-operation in Sweden and Norway, denying talk that it had withdrawn from talks.

"There is nothing new to report about the negotiations, they are continuing quietly and in a positive tone," Carlsberg director Walter Poulsen told Reuters in response to a Norwegian press report that Carlsberg had quit the talks with Coca Cola.
Carlsberg and two Norwegian brewers, Macks Bryggerier and Borg Bryggerier, seeks to buy former Coke producer Hansa, from Scandinavian producer Pripps Ringnes.
The U.S. beverage giant and Pripps Ringnes agreed in June to end their co-operation agreement in Norway and Sweden.
"We made an informal takeover bid for Hansa along with the two Norwegian brewers back in May and that is where we stand today," Poulsen said.
"After that (Macks and Borg) made their own independent offer in full agreement with Carlsberg. Both offers are still on the table but we've heard nothing," he added.
Analysts see Carlsberg winning the Coca Cola licenses in both Norway and Sweden, bringing in new annual pre-tax income for the group of 50-100 million Danish crowns.
European Union competition authorities have instructed Pripps Ringnes-owner Orkla to sell Hansa by the end of 1997.
Carlsberg already produces and markets Coca Cola products in Denmark. --Joern Nurkka, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
